films.name: Kodacolor 100

origin.note: Announced by Kodak in October 2025. Its parent emulsion is not documented in this library.

films.history: Kodacolor was Kodak's consumer colour negative name from 1942. The 1972 to 1980s C-41 Kodacolor films are separate records in this library. Kodak announced a Kodacolor 100 and a Kodacolor 200 in October 2025, both 35 mm C-41 films rated at 100 and 200 speed. Which existing emulsion the 100 is cut from is not documented here.
films.notes: The name is current. The emulsion's origin is not documented.

films.name: Kodacolor 200

origin.note: Announced by Kodak in October 2025. Its parent emulsion is not documented in this library and is not assumed to be Gold 200.

films.history: Announced with the Kodacolor 100 in October 2025 as a 35 mm C-41 film rated at 200 speed. It is a separate product from the 1980s Kodacolor 200 records in this library, which share its name. Its parent emulsion is not documented here.
films.notes: Shares a name with the 1980s Kodacolor 200 records. The generation label is what tells them apart.

films.name: UltraMax 800
films.history: UltraMax 800 is Kodak's 800-speed consumer colour negative. This library does not yet hold a source for its dates or its current availability, so none are stated here.
films.notes: Current status and availability have not been checked against a source.

films.name: Portra 100T
films.history: Portra 100T was the tungsten-balanced member of Kodak's original Portra family, colour-corrected for about 3200 K so that interiors and night work under incandescent light needed no 80A filter. It was a C-41 negative film like the rest of the range, with the soft contrast and gentle skin tones the family is known for, and it was discontinued in the 2000s as Kodak consolidated Portra. Shot in daylight without an 85B filter it goes strongly blue.

characteristics.label: Balance
characteristics.value: Tungsten, about 3200 K. Daylight needs an 85B filter, or a deliberate blue cast.

characteristics.label: Process
characteristics.value: C-41. It is a negative film, not an E-6 slide stock, despite the tungsten balance.

films.name: Vista Plus 100

origin.note: The published list of discontinued films describes it as a rebranded Fujicolor Superia 100.

films.history: Vista Plus 100 was sold under the AgfaPhoto name from 2009 to 2018. Ferrania stopped making AgfaPhoto colour film in 2009, and the published list describes Vista Plus 100 as a rebranded Fujicolor Superia 100, made in Japan. Production ended in 2018.

characteristics.label: What it really is
characteristics.value: Rebranded Fujicolor Superia 100, per the published list.

films.name: Vista Plus 200

origin.note: Sold in 24 and 36 exposure rolls and in three-packs. Production ended in 2018, with the last stock dated April 2020, per the published list.

films.history: Vista Plus 200 is listed as a rebranded Fujicolor Superia 200. It was sold in 24 and 36 exposure rolls and in three-packs, production ended in 2018, and the published list gives a last stock expiry of April 2020.

characteristics.label: What it really is
characteristics.value: Rebranded Fujicolor Superia 200, per the published list.

characteristics.label: Expired stock
characteristics.value: Last stock dated April 2020, per the published list.

films.name: Vista Plus 400

origin.note: The published list says the 400 is assumed to be Fujicolor Superia 400. It is not documented.

films.history: Vista Plus 400 was sold from 2009 to 2018. The published list says it is assumed to be Fujicolor Superia 400. That is not documented, so it stays an assumption here.

characteristics.label: What it probably is
characteristics.value: Superia 400, by inference from its siblings. Not documented.
